blocks.prompt: 3. The nth terms of the sequences \(1, 2, 4, 8, \ldots\) and \(256, 128, 64, \ldots\) are equal. Find the value of \(n\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do G.P. hain: pehli har dafa double ho rahi hai, doosri har dafa aadhi. Ek barh rahi hai, ek ghat rahi hai, to kahin na kahin dono ka term barabar ho jayega.
Diya kya hai? Dono sequences.
Find kya karna hai? Woh position \(n\) jahan dono ke nth terms barabar hon.
Plan: dono ka nth term 2 ki power ki shakal mein likhenge, barabar rakhenge, aur powers compare karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(1, 2, 4, 8, \ldots\) aur \(256, 128, 64, \ldots\)
Humein find karna hai: \(n\), jahan nth terms barabar hon.
Tareeqa: Har sequence ke liye \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) likhenge. Phir dono nth terms ki equation (muadla) banayenge. Yeh tareeqa is liye theek hai ke \(n\) dono formulas mein power ki jagah aata hai, aur same base hone par powers compare ho sakti hain.

Pehli sequence ka nth term
\[a_1 = 1,\ r = 2\]
\[a_n = 1 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^{n-1}\]
Kyun: \(2/1 = 2\), \(4/2 = 2\): har term pichle ka do guna hai, is liye \(r = 2\). 1 se multiply karne se kuch nahi badalta.

Doosri sequence ka nth term
\[a_1 = 256,\ r = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[a_n = 256\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[= \dfrac{2^{8}}{2^{n-1}} = 2^{9-n}\]
Kyun: \(128/256 = \frac{1}{2}\), yani har term aadha ho raha hai. Ab dono terms ko ek hi base 2 mein lana zaroori hai, is liye \(256 = 2^8\) likha (\(2^8 = 256\) yaad rakhiye). \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1} = \frac{1}{2^{n-1}}\), aur divide karne par powers minus hoti hain: \(8 - (n - 1) = 9 - n\).
Dhyan dein: \(8 - (n - 1)\) mein bracket kholte waqt \(+1\) banta hai, \(-1\) nahi.

Barabar rakh kar \(n\) nikalein
\[2^{n-1} = 2^{9-n}\]
\[n - 1 = 9 - n\]
\[2n = 10 \Rightarrow n = 5\]
Kyun: Jab do barabar numbers ek hi base (jo 0, 1 ya \(-1\) na ho) ki powers hon, to un ki powers bhi barabar hoti hain. Is se ek aasaan linear equation bani: dono taraf \(n\) jama kiya aur 1 jama kiya to \(2n = 10\).

Tasdeeq: dono ke 5th terms
\[1, 2, 4, 8, 16\]
\[256, 128, 64, 32, 16\]
Kyun: Dono lists ka paanchwan term 16 hai. Is ke baad pehli sequence 32 aur doosri 8 par chali jati hai, is liye sirf \(n = 5\) par hi dono barabar hain.
